title: How Waterfalls Carve Canyons in Solid Rock

media.title: File:Mt Nimrod Scenic Reserve - Waterfall on Nimrod Stream (video).webm
File:A train running over Vintgar Gorge, Slovenia.webm

script: How do plunging rivers actually carve solid rock? Niagara Falls moves backward four feet every year. Falling water traps air and blasts canyon walls with millions of tiny shockwaves. This process, called cavitation, shatters stone from the inside out. Over thousands of years, the churning water eats away the softer layers underneath. Eventually, the heavy caprock collapses, forcing the entire waterfall to retreat upstream. This relentless erosion slices deep canyons into the Earth.
